analysis.title: eToro Group (ETOR): First take: Slightly better adj. expenses, but weaker ECC quarterly results, and October run rate
key_insights: ETOR reported 3Q26 EPS of 14c, below GSe/Visible Alpha consensus of 27c/23c. Adjusted EPS (ex-SBC) was 26c, below GSe/consensus of 33c/29c.

GS expects a muted reaction. Modestly better adjusted expenses are likely to be overshadowed by weaker net contribution in the quarter (weaker ECC, partly offset by stronger Crypto, both vs. the Street) and by October trends that imply lower 4Q26E ECC and crypto activity than GSe/consensus.

Net contribution was 1% below the Street. eToro Money, ECC and Subscription & other were 13%, 11% and 42% lower. Crypto net contribution was 85% higher and net interest contribution 2% higher. Adjusted expenses were 1% below the Street.
Adjusted pre-tax margin was 17.3%, about 35bps below Street estimates and down about 16.7pp QoQ.

3Q26 ECC revenue per trade was $0.60 versus GSe/Street of $0.67/$0.64. The crypto take rate was 1.87% versus GSe/Street of 0.90%/0.89%. GS says much of the sequential rise may reflect positive crypto mark-to-market.
ETOR disclosed about $13mn of corporate crypto treasury holdings at end of 2Q26. With 41% crypto market cap appreciation over the quarter, GS implies $5.3mn of marks.
Run-rating October ECC trades for the full quarter implies 140mn trades, 19%/18% below the 4Q26 Street/GSe of 172mn/170mn and down about 5% QoQ.
Run-rating October crypto volumes (trades x invested amount per trade) implies $1.3bn, below 4Q26 consensus/GSe of $2.0bn/$1.7bn and down 8% QoQ.
ECC net contribution was $88.5mn, down 38% QoQ and 11% below the Street, on 7% lower net trading contribution per trade and 4% fewer ECC trades, both vs. the Street.
Crypto net contribution was $26.3mn, up 139% QoQ and 85% above consensus. Crypto volumes were 11% below the Street, offset by a take rate 96bps higher.

Net interest contribution was $50mn, up 2% QoQ and 2% above the Street, on a 9bps higher NIM partly offset by 1% lower average earning assets. Interest earning assets were $7.0bn at 3Q26 versus $7.9bn at 3Q25.
eToro Money contribution was $20mn, down 23% QoQ and 13% below consensus, on a 3bps lower effective fee rate and 9% lower total money transfers.
September/October ECC trades were 46.7mn/48.2mn (-10%/+3% MoM). Crypto trades were 2.4mn/2.0mn (-55%/-17% MoM).

Net new accounts were 30k in each of September and October. Total funded accounts were 4.42mn in October, up 8% MoM annualized and 18% YoY (10% YoY adjusted for the Zengo, Bit2C and Spaceship acquisitions). Management guides to double-digit annual funded account growth over time.

ETOR announced the acquisition of LB Finanzas, a digital investment and payment platform in Argentina. GS also flags that metrics for the TradeZero acquisition, announced at 2Q26 results, were not previously disclosed.

GS wants clarity on October ECC and 3Q26 volume drivers and the retail trading outlook, sizing of the LB Finanzas and TradeZero customer bases and revenue, drivers of the weaker ECC take rates, and the near-term crypto volume and take rate outlook.
GS rates ETOR Neutral with a $29 12-month price target, based on 7.0x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS ex-SBC. The stock closed at $23.32 on 9 Nov 2026, implying 24.4% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral and $29 target maintained after 3Q26 results. EPS missed, October ECC and crypto run rates are below consensus, and funded account growth of 8% annualized in October is below management's double-digit guidance.

earnings_insights: ETOR 3Q26 reported EPS 14c versus GSe 27c and Visible Alpha consensus 23c (consensus EPS calculated by GS from consensus P&L components). Reported 11/10/2026.
ETOR 3Q26 adjusted EPS ex-SBC 26c versus GSe 33c and consensus 29c. Reported 11/10/2026.
3Q26 adjusted pre-tax margin 17.3% versus Street about 35bps higher, down about 16.7pp QoQ.

3Q26 net contribution was 1% below the Street. ECC was 11% lower, eToro Money 13% lower and Subscription & other 42% lower. Crypto was 85% higher and net interest 2% higher. Adjusted expenses were 1% below the Street, with G&A 11% lower.
October-implied run rate for 4Q26: ECC trades of 140mn versus Street 172mn and GSe 170mn (estimates). Crypto volume of $1.3bn versus consensus $2.0bn and GSe $1.7bn (estimates).

GS FY estimates: EPS $2.55 for 12/26E, $3.59 for 12/27E and $4.37 for 12/28E. Quarterly EPS: $0.33 for 9/26E (GS estimate before the print), $0.61 for 12/26E and $0.70 for 3/27E. Revenue is $902.8mn for 12/26E and $1,068.3mn for 12/27E (GS estimates).
crypto_views: ETOR crypto net contribution of $26.3mn was up 139% QoQ and 85% above consensus, helped by a 1.87% take rate versus GSe/Street of 0.90%/0.89%. GS says much of the sequential rise may reflect positive crypto mark-to-market on corporate holdings.
Crypto trades fell 55% MoM in September to 2.4mn and 17% MoM in October to 2.0mn. Run-rated October crypto volume implies $1.3bn for 4Q26, 8% below 3Q and below consensus $2.0bn and GSe $1.7bn.
risk_factors: Downside risks: unsuccessful US expansion, a slowdown in the retail trading cycle, a crypto market downturn, and substantially lower interest rates.
Upside risks: faster and cheaper US expansion, CopyTrader proving more differentiated and harder to replicate than expected, and a renewed acceleration in crypto trading.
October ECC and crypto activity are well below consensus, and funded account growth of 8% annualized is below management's double-digit guidance.
